question: A car travels four consecutive distances of 2 km each at speeds of 10 km/hr, 20 km/hr, 30 km/hr, and 40 km/hr, respectively. What is the average speed of the car (in km/hr) over this total distance?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For equal consecutive distances, the average speed is independent of the actual distance length.

Assume the distance of each part = LCM(10, 20, 30, 40) = 120 km.

Total distance = 4 parts × 120 km = 480 km.

Total time taken = (120÷10) + (120÷20) + (120÷30) + (120÷40) = 12 + 6 + 4 + 3 = 25 hours.

Average speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time = 480 ÷ 25 = 19.2 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 19.2 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance of each consecutive part = 2 km.

Speeds for each respective part = 10 km/hr, 20 km/hr, 30 km/hr, 40 km/hr.

 Total Distance = 8 km

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total Distance = 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8 km

⇒ Time for 1st part = 2 ÷ 10 = 1/5 hr

⇒ Time for 2nd part = 2 ÷ 20 = 1/10 hr

⇒ Time for 3rd part = 2 ÷ 30 = 1/15 hr

⇒ Time for 4th part = 2 ÷ 40 = 1/20 hr

⇒ Total Time = 1/5 + 1/10 + 1/15 + 1/20

⇒ LCM of denominators (5, 10, 15, 20) is 60.

⇒ Total Time = (12 + 6 + 4 + 3) ÷ 60 = 25/60 = 5/12 hr

⇒ Average Speed = 8 ÷ (5/12)

⇒ Average Speed = (8 × 12) ÷ 5 = 96 ÷ 5 = 19.2 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 19.2 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed General Formula

Average Speed is always calculated as Total Distance divided by Total Time. Never take the arithmetic mean of the individual speeds unless the time intervals spent traveling at each speed are equal.

Average Speed for Two Equal Distances

If an object covers two equal distances at speeds x and y, the average speed is given by the harmonic mean: Average Speed = (2xy) ÷ (x + y).

Average Speed for Three Equal Distances

If an object covers three equal consecutive distances at speeds x, y, and z, the average speed is calculated as: Average Speed = (3xyz) ÷ (xy + yz + zx).
